[LEXP.3.9.2] **Correctly rounded.** For every operand, the engine must return
the function's exact mathematical value rounded once to the nearest `float64`,
ties to even ([LDET.3.6.1]): an overflowing value rounds to an infinity and an
underflowing one to a subnormal or a zero, as any rounding does. The compiler
must do the same wherever it evaluates one ([LDET.3.3a.7]). An implementation
whose result differs from that value at any operand must not be used.

The rounded value is unique, so every conforming engine returns the same bits at
every operand that has one ([LDET.3.4.1]). At the operands where the function
has no real value, or its value is a limit, the result is [LEXP.3.9.3]'s.
